project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas xeric cliffbrake reference module
project_scope.note: Built around purple cliffbrake-style frond and sori architecture.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Ignore flowers entirely. Read the frond, then turn a fertile frond over and inspect the margins for sori.
family_diagnostics.frond: Stipe below the blade, rachis through the blade, divided into pinnae/pinnules/segments depending on species.
family_diagnostics.sori: Many local cheilanthoids have marginal/submarginal sori protected by the rolled blade margin as a false indusium.
family_diagnostics.reproduction: Spores, not seeds; no flowers or fruits.
family_diagnostics.habitat: Many local species occupy dry limestone or rock crevices.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Regular marginal sori + rolled leaf edge is far more useful than assuming every fern needs wet shade.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Central Texas cliffbrakes are a perfect reminder that ferns can be dry-rock plants—and that the underside of the frond is where the ID lives.

steps.title: 1 · Start with a purple cliffbrake
steps.look_for: Dark rachis with divided leathery frond segments.
steps.why_it_matters: Provides a strong xeric Pteridaceae field gestalt.

steps.title: 2 · Put it in a dry-rock habitat
steps.look_for: A fern growing from a dry mineral crevice rather than wet forest soil.

steps.title: 3 · Flip the frond over
steps.look_for: Regular bands/clusters of sporangia near the segment margins.
steps.why_it_matters: Sorus placement is a major fern-family and genus character.

steps.title: 4 · Find the false indusium
steps.look_for: The blade edge rolls over the sori; the covering is leaf tissue, not a separate membrane.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the classic cheilanthoid/Pteridaceae teaching structure.

comparisons.title: False vs true indusium
comparisons.rule: A false indusium is the rolled blade margin; a true indusium is a separate membrane covering the sorus.

comparisons.title: Fern vs flowering plant
comparisons.rule: Pteridaceae has spores and sporangia, never flowers, fruits, or seeds.

visual_lesson.caveat: False indusia are common in our local cliffbrake framework but are not universal across the enormous Pteridaceae family.

video_handoff.policy: Use the exact fertile-frond frame to strengthen the sori/pseudoindusium lesson while keeping the species range-pending.
